chapters.title: Summary
chapters.summary: What the formal text claims, the ideas that carry the proof and where they live, how the reading was done, what it does not establish, and how to read it. It names the four quoted results that have no identified published counterpart in the form needed: a prime d whose quadratic twists have no zero in a box for all characters at once, a uniform odd-Sha bound for abelian CM fields, a finite detecting set of Galois elements, and relations at split primes.

chapters.summary: The twists: one per embedding, chosen on the Galois side so that the ℓ-adic denominators of the projection to theta lifts stay within budget. Congruences give Selmer classes by Ribet's method; one anticyclotomic twist makes all Selmer groups short for m powers at once; Taylor–Wiles primes are added one at a time; the loss at ℓ is controlled through Kisin modules.

title: The condensed Lean proof of RH and GRH: a reading
byline: riemann-rev · first handout, working draft of 26 November 2026 · readers, writer and referees are AI systems (Claude agents, with an independent AI second reader) · [online PDF](https://nasqret.github.io/riemann-rev/writeup/handout.pdf)
note: PDF page = printed page + 1. The handout reads the **compact edition** of lsernau/grh-lean (`grh-compact`, commit 72fead1), the Claude-written rewrite of Alpöge's proof, unit by unit from the final theorems down. Its own numbering is odd: the eight chapters are I–VIII, and the 47 notes inside them are numbered 0.1–0.47. Each note opens with a summary and a box saying what it proves in full and what it takes as input, and every statement carries a LEAN line naming the declarations it renders. **Read with care:** no human mathematician has refereed it. The handout says plainly that the program check compares quotations and arguments with the source, not their meaning; that the independent kernel build and the dependency export were still pending on 26 November; that the 2,944 background results are quoted rather than read, with 113 compared against a published source; and that four quoted results have no identified published counterpart in the form needed (see the Summary). Each chapter and section below links to its page in the [online PDF](https://nasqret.github.io/riemann-rev/writeup/handout.pdf) and gives its range in the Drive copy. For the original archive and the earlier Dupuy notes, see [Notes on Alpöge's Proof](https://vwulf.github.io/ettuge/Deep-Dives/textbooks/alpoge-riemann-hypothesis-notes) and [Math Deep Dives › RH](https://vwulf.github.io/ettuge/Deep-Dives/math/ch3#rh-rewrite). Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A 1,353-page mathematical reading of the 113,000-line compact Lean proof of RH and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, produced by AI agents that rewrote each of the code's 24 units as mathematics from 986 program-checked structured proofs. The argument runs top-down: A, B and C give the main inequality, the main inequality gives a one-sided bound for primes, that bound gives the zero-free half-plane, and the half-plane gives the five theorems. Primes enter through a remainder R(x) of a weighted prime sum that counts only primes not split in K = ℚ(√−d). Because zeros of L(s, ξ) and of the twists L(s, ξχ_K) enter its Laplace transform with opposite signs, Landau's theorem on non-negative functions turns an *upper* bound R(x) ≤ x^(8ε−1/2) into a zero-free half-plane; the prime d is chosen so its twists have no zeros in a box. The bound comes from one covolume bounded from two sides over a CM field E = K(ζ). Theorem A says Poincaré series of ramified columns have short, nearly integral images under a chain of m ≈ √x theta lifts (via a seesaw identity and the divisibility of jets of CM theta functions at non-split primes). Theorem B says few translates of these Poincaré series span almost all rows (a Petersson-type second moment with Bessel functions and a sieve). Theorem C says integral forms cannot be that short (lift volumes as Hecke L-values, an exchange identity, heights indexed by embeddings, twists chosen through Selmer groups by Ribet's method, Taylor–Wiles primes and Kisin modules). The main amounts cancel and the saving x^(−1/2) is 1/m. The handout ends with a catalogue of the 2,944 quoted background declarations and a record of who checked what.
